rubrics.justification: The response overcalls the embryo as a good-quality expanded/full blastocyst with a well-formed blastocoel. In the image, expansion appears limited/collapsed and ICM/TE are poorly defined; claims of relatively numerous cohesive TE and a well-formed cavity are not well supported.

It integrates age, BMI, ovarian reserve, male factor, endometrium, prior cycle history, and lifestyle factors with prognosis reasonably well, though some links to embryo-specific quality are somewhat generic.
The structure is logical overall, but the implantation estimate is optimistic given the uncertain/likely suboptimal morphology and the morphology discussion itself contains unsupported assumptions.

Recommendations such as SET and standard luteal support are broadly guideline-consistent, but suggesting PGT-A after one unsuccessful transfer in a 34-year-old male-factor case is more debatable and not clearly guideline-driven; morphology grading application is also loose.
Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, lifestyle counseling, and contingency planning, though some advice remains general rather than embryo-specific.
